html:
The French colony of Upper Volta, carved out of French West Africa on 1 March 1919, with its capital at Ouagadougou. It is the territory of today's Burkina Faso.

France saw it mainly as a reserve of workers. In 1932 the colony was abolished and split among Ivory Coast, French Sudan and Niger, partly so its people could be sent to plantations and building sites in those colonies. The Mogho Naba of the Mossi and local leaders pressed for its return, and it was restored in 1947. It became independent as the Republic of Upper Volta on 5 August 1960, and Thomas Sankara renamed it Burkina Faso in 1984. See also Mossi migration.
